chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a man, from Ali, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marar, from Yunus, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who enters Mecca once, twice, or four times in a year, what should he do? He said: When he enters, he should enter in the state of Talbiyah (Muhrim), and when he leaves, he should leave in the state of Ihlal (not having performed Umrah to end the Ihram). He said: And for every month, there is an Umrah. I asked: Will that be less? He said: It will be an Umrah for every ten days. Then he said: And by your right, indeed in this year of mine, there were six Umrahs. I asked: Why is that? He said: I was with Muhammad ibn Ibrahim in al-Ta'if, and whenever he entered, I entered with him.

key_terms.مُحِلّاً: In the state of Ihlal (free from the restrictions of Ihram)
key_terms.مُلَبِّياً: In the state of Talbiyah (reciting the talbiyah formula upon entering Ihram)

ai.seo_question: How many times can one perform Umrah in a year according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* clarifies the permissibility of performing multiple Umrahs within a single year, with the Imam specifying a frequency of one Umrah every ten days. The narration highlights the practical application of this ruling through the Imam’s personal experience of performing six Umrahs in one year while residing in al-Ta'if, demonstrating that repeated pilgrimage is not only allowed but can be a regular devotional practice.
